title: What can you say about Panax ginseng in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 3 wordings for Panax ginseng; the strongest is "Used in herbal medicine to help support cognitive function and reduce mental fatigue" (moderate, 200-600 mg standardized extract a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats erectile dysfunction".

supported_wordings.wording: Used in herbal medicine to help support cognitive function and reduce mental fatigue.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it as a herbal medicine use at 200-600 mg of standardized extract a day; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada: 200-600 mg of extract a day standardized to 4-7% ginsenosides, or 0.5-9 g of dried root a day.
supported_wordings.form: Root extract, standardized to 4-7% total ginsenosides

wordings_to_avoid.why: Presents the product as a drug.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
